issues.display_title: Issue #481: Sync Live Schema to Dev
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 24/08/26

✅ Implementation: Sync Live Schema to Dev

Goal: Prepare and validate migrations that sync ten tables and 24 views before applying them to live, adding only what live is missing.

Architecture: This sync owns eleven versioned SQL files. The active top-level directory contains 20 migrations total; the runner applies all unapplied files in filename order. The ten schema-sync files run before the final view rebuild, which drops and recreates 24 views in dependency order inside one explicit transaction.

Tech Stack: CockroachDB, cmd/migrate (pgx), SQL

Task spec: docs/tasks/2026-08-24/sync_live_schema_to_dev.md

Global Constraints

  • Add only. No column, index, or constraint that exists on live and not on dev may be dropped.
  • No CASCADE on any view drop.
  • Table migrations must be applied before the view rebuild.
  • Normal column and index statements in the eleven sync files are guarded where CockroachDB supports it. Historical top-level migrations and marked ADD CONSTRAINT statements are not all re-runnable.

Migration Files

Applied in filename order.

File Contents
2026082401_users.sql 11 columns (ban/report fields, cover_image, cover_path, city, website) and indexes users_email_idx, idx_users_search, idx_users_id_banned
2026082402_posts.sql 10 columns (ban/report fields, location_group, location_group_slug, affiliate_id), two column comments, six indexes including an inverted trigram index, and the posts_affiliate_fk foreign key; scoring columns remain owned by 20260821_recommendation_scores.sql
2026082403_comment.sql Seven moderation columns: banned, banned_reason, banned_at, restore_reason, restore_at, report_reason, report_at
2026082404_bookmark.sql Indexes only: idx_bookmark_folder_created_at, idx_bookmark_post_id, unique bookmark_user_post_key
2026082405_folder_bookmark.sql Six columns (is_published, published_at, description, location, location_name, category_id), partial index idx_folder_bookmark_published_slug, and the folder_bookmark_category_fk foreign key
2026082406_error_log.sql Drops error_log_user_id_fkey, then drops NOT NULL on user_id
2026082407_report_issue_comment.sql Column status INT2 DEFAULT 0 and its comment
2026082408_report_issue_post.sql Column status, its comment, and index idx_report_post_status_post
2026082409_report_issue_user.sql Column status, its comment, and index idx_report_issue_user_status_user
2026082410_user_detail.sql Five onboarding columns and the discovery_source / usage_intent check constraints
2026082413_views_rebuild.sql Drops and recreates all 24 views in one transaction

Current top-level runner order:

202608012_create_affiliate_categories.sql
202608013_create_affiliate.sql
20260805_add_user_cover.sql
20260806_add_profile_v2.sql
20260807_add_bookmark_user_post_unique.sql
20260808_create_user_activity_logs.sql
20260809_create_shares.sql
20260810_post_hotspots.sql
20260821_recommendation_scores.sql
2026082401_users.sql
2026082402_posts.sql
2026082403_comment.sql
2026082404_bookmark.sql
2026082405_folder_bookmark.sql
2026082406_error_log.sql
2026082407_report_issue_comment.sql
2026082408_report_issue_post.sql
2026082409_report_issue_user.sql
2026082410_user_detail.sql
2026082413_views_rebuild.sql

There is guarded schema overlap with historical migrations: 2026082401_users.sql repeats
cover_image / cover_path from 20260805 and city / website from 20260806 using
IF NOT EXISTS; 2026082404_bookmark.sql repeats the unique key created by 20260807 as
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS. The five recommendation-score columns have no overlap and remain
owned only by 20260821_recommendation_scores.sql.

Design Notes

Idempotency. Schema-sync columns use ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, indexes use CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS.
CockroachDB does not accept IF NOT EXISTS on ADD CONSTRAINT, so the four constraint statements
(posts_affiliate_fk, folder_bookmark_category_fk, and the two user_detail check constraints)
sit in marked blocks at the end of their files. Before applying, compare existing constraints by name
and definition. Do not permanently remove a matching constraint statement from repository history;
reconcile the target ledger/schema or use a reviewed deployment copy if an operational skip is needed.

Ordinary migrations are not atomic as a whole. The runner executes statements one at a time and
records the version afterward. If a statement fails, earlier statements in that file can remain while
the version stays unrecorded. Retrying then starts that file again.

View rebuild. CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW fails whenever the column list or column order changes,
and several of these views changed both, so every view is dropped first and recreated. No CASCADE:
if an unlisted view on live depends on one being dropped, the statement must fail loudly rather than
silently delete that dependent. views_published_folder_posts depends on views_timeline_post_slim,
so it is dropped first and created last. views_total_posts_per_user is referenced by
followers_counts but did not change, so it is not rebuilt and stays in place. The file is wrapped
in BEGIN / COMMIT so a failure halfway cannot leave a view dropped with no replacement.

splitSQLStatements in cmd/migrate/main.go splits on ; and executes each statement separately on
the same connection, so BEGIN and COMMIT run as ordinary statements. The transaction still holds;
the runner is simply unaware it is inside one. The ledger insert happens after COMMIT; if that insert
fails, all view DDL is committed but version 2026082413 remains unrecorded.

Version numbering. parseMigration requires VERSION_name.sql and rejects the entire run if any
file in migrations/*.sql does not match, so plain names like users.sql are not usable. Versions
must also be unique. Versions 2026082401 through 2026082410, followed by 2026082413, keep the
ten table changes ahead of the view rebuild. String sorting places 20260824 before
2026082401 — a plain-date views file would run before the columns it selects exist.

Duplicate Migration Versions

The conflicting historical files were renamed or moved so active top-level versions are unique:

20260808_create_affiliate_categories.sql -> 202608012_create_affiliate_categories.sql
20260809_create_affiliate.sql -> 202608013_create_affiliate.sql
20260806_create_user_activity_logs.sql -> 20260808_create_user_activity_logs.sql
20260806_create_shares.sql -> 20260809_create_shares.sql
20260807_update_views_timeline_post_v2.sql -> migrations/views/2026082411_update_views_timeline_post_v2.sql
20260807_update_views_place_list_categories.sql -> migrations/views/2026082412_update_views_place_list_categories.sql
2026082411_views_rebuild.sql -> 2026082413_views_rebuild.sql

Content from 20260811_shares.sql, 20260811_user_social_links.sql, and
20260812_make_error_log_user_id_nullable.sql was consolidated into active canonical migrations.
Files under migrations/views/ are not loaded by cmd/migrate; the directory contains 24 canonical
view definitions plus two moved historical reference files (2026082411_* and 2026082412_*).

Before live deployment, compare public.schema_migrations with the actual schema. The ledger keys
only on version; renaming an already-applied migration can otherwise rerun its DDL or skip different
content that reused the same historical version.

Pre-Migration Data Checks

Check bookmark duplicates

SELECT user_id, post_id, COUNT(*) AS total
FROM bookmark
GROUP BY user_id, post_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

Expected: no rows. bookmark_user_post_key cannot be created otherwise. Remove duplicates first if
any appear.

Confirm the affiliate table exists

2026082402_posts.sql adds a foreign key to public.affiliate, created by
202608013_create_affiliate.sql. Confirm it is present on live before running.

List views that depend on the rebuild set

Any view on live outside the 24 that references one of them will make the drop fail. Identify them
now so the failure is not a surprise mid-run.

Confirm external view prerequisites

public.views_total_posts_per_user and public.places_not_used must exist before 2026082413 runs.
Neither relation is created by the active top-level migrations or bootstrap schema. Import their live
DDL into a fresh dev/test database; on live, verify the existing definitions instead of replacing them.

Applying Migrations

Run the migrator

$env:MIGRATE_DSN_DEV = 'postgresql://USER:PASSWORD@HOST:26257/DATABASE?sslmode=require'
go run ./cmd/migrate -target=dev -- up

The runner processes every unapplied top-level migration in filename order, including
2026082401 through 2026082410 and the final 2026082413 view rebuild, then records each
completed version in schema_migrations.

Handle the constraint blocks

If a run stops on posts_affiliate_fk, folder_bookmark_category_fk, or a user_detail check
constraint because it already exists, first confirm the existing constraint has the same definition.
Because earlier statements may already have applied without a ledger record, reconcile the target
state before retrying. Do not permanently delete the constraint from the canonical migration.

Verify columns against the snapshots

Every column, index, and constraint in the Dev section of each file under
migrations/schema_snapshots/ must now exist on live. Nothing that was in the Live section may be
gone, except error_log_user_id_fkey.

View Rebuild

2026082413_views_rebuild.sql runs automatically in the same migrator invocation after all table
migrations. It is not a separate cmd/migrate phase.

Expected: 24 drops and 24 creates commit together. The later ledger insert is outside this transaction.

On failure, confirm nothing was lost

The transaction rolls back as a unit. Verify all 24 views still exist, fix the reported dependency or
column error, then re-run.

Smoke-check each view

SELECT * FROM <view> LIMIT 1 for all 24. Missing relations or columns normally fail during
CREATE VIEW; smoke queries verify the created views can be queried against actual target data.

Confirm untouched views survived

views_total_posts_per_user, and every other view outside the rebuild list, must still exist. Their
absence would mean a drop cascaded.

Verification Status

Static/unit tests in cmd/migrate/main_test.go check that table migrations run before the view rebuild, top-level
migrations contain no hardcoded panorra_dev, panorra_test, or panorra_live qualifier, and
20260821_recommendation_scores.sql is the sole owner of the five recommendation-score columns.
They do not integration-test CockroachDB transactions, partial retries, ledger compatibility, or the
live schema.

go test ./cmd/migrate -count=1
ok   panorra-api-new/cmd/migrate

The dev migration trial applied the table migrations, then stopped at 2026082413 because the new
test database does not contain public.views_total_posts_per_user. The view rebuild also expects
public.places_not_used. The 2026082413 transaction rolled back, while previously completed
migrations stayed applied. Export both definitions from live and import them into dev/test before
retrying; verify they already exist on live before deployment.

Before live deployment, verify posts.scored_at exists if ledger version 20260821 is already
recorded; the ledger stores no migration checksum.

Scope

  • Bring the live database schema up to the dev schema for ten tables and all 24 rebuilt views.
  • Add only what live is missing. Never drop a column, index, or constraint that live has and dev does not.
  • Ship the change as versioned migration files that cmd/migrate can load and apply in order.
  • Keep the raw Live / Dev schema snapshots as reference material, outside the migration path.

Tables In Scope

users, posts, comment, bookmark, folder_bookmark, error_log, report_issue_comment,
report_issue_post, report_issue_user, user_detail.

Source of Truth

Each table had a snapshot file holding both the live and the dev CREATE TABLE output. Those
snapshots live in migrations/schema_snapshots/ and are not read by the runner:

migrations/schema_snapshots/
    bookmark  comment  error_log.txt  folder_bookmark  posts
    report_issue_comment  report_issue_post  report_issue_user  user_detail  users

View definitions live in migrations/views/ as 24 individual .sql files, already rewritten to
reference panorra_live. They are reference copies; the runner does not read subdirectories.

Requirements

  • Every migration is re-runnable. Objects live already has must be skipped, not raise an error.
  • Views are dropped and recreated, never replaced in place, because their column lists and column
    order changed.
  • A view drop must never cascade. If an unlisted view on live depends on one being dropped, the
    run has to fail rather than delete it.
  • Table changes must be applied before the view rebuild, since the new views select columns the
    table migrations add.
  • Filenames must satisfy parseMigration: VERSION_name.sql, with a version unique across
    migrations/*.sql.

Deliberately Not Changed

Live carries indexes that dev does not. None are dropped:

  • comment: comment_parent_slug_user_id_post_id_idx, comment_parent_slug_user_id_post_id_idx1, comment_parent_slug_user_id_idx
  • user_detail: user_detail_user_id_idx, user_detail_user_id_idx1
  • users: users_email_unique, users_username_unique
  • posts: posts_slug_idx, posts_slug_idx1, posts_slug_idx2, posts_is_publish_slug_idx, posts_slug_is_publish_idx, posts_user_id_rec_idx

posts.visibility differs only by database name in its enum type
(panorra_live.public.post_visibility against panorra_dev.public.post_visibility). That is not a
schema difference and needs no migration.

Pre-Migration Checks

The unique index on bookmark (user_id, post_id) cannot be created while duplicates exist:

SELECT user_id, post_id, COUNT(*) AS total
FROM bookmark
GROUP BY user_id, post_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

The posts migration adds a foreign key to public.affiliate, which must already exist from
20260809_create_affiliate.sql.

Known Blocker

cmd/migrate cannot complete a run today because three older versions are duplicated:

  • 20260806 — add_profile_v2, create_shares, create_user_activity_logs
  • 20260807 — add_bookmark_user_post_unique, update_views_place_list_categories, update_views_timeline_post_v2
  • 20260811 — shares, user_social_links

This predates the files in this task. loadMigrations returns an error on a duplicate version
before a single statement executes, so the run aborts entirely.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Every column, index, and constraint present in the dev snapshot exists on live.
  • No column, index, or constraint that live had before the migration was removed, except
    error_log_user_id_fkey, which dev does not have.
  • All 24 views exist on live and select without error.
  • views_total_posts_per_user, and every other view outside the rebuild list, is untouched.
  • Re-running any migration file makes no further change, apart from the marked ADD CONSTRAINT
    blocks.

Implementation

See docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-24-sync-live-schema-to-dev.md.
